links.outcome: Physician diagnostic sensitivity, confidence and trust with versus without model-assisted enhanced-audio workflow
links.effect: Workflows integrating enhanced audio gave an 11.61% increase in diagnostic sensitivity, with improved efficiency, diagnostic confidence, and trust.
links.quote: Quantitative analysis from the physician validation study revealed improvements in efficiency, diagnostic confidence, and trust during model-assisted diagnosis, with workflows that integrated enhanced audio leading to an 11.61% increase in diagnostic sensitivity and facilitating high-confidence diagnoses.

links.outcome: Respiratory sound classification performance under noisy input, with and without audio enhancement
links.effect: Audio enhancement gave a 21.88% increase in ICBHI score (P<.001) on ICBHI and a 4.1% improvement (P<.001) on Formosa in multi-class noisy scenarios.
links.quote: The integration of the audio enhancement module resulted in a 21.88% increase with P<.001 in the ICBHI classification score on the ICBHI dataset and a 4.1% improvement with P<.001 on the Formosa Archive of Breath Sound dataset in multi-class noisy scenarios.

unlisted_practices: Deep learning-based audio enhancement preprocessing to improve robustness of classification to noise

screen.reason: Evaluates an audio enhancement preprocessing guardrail/practice to improve robustness against real-world noise in automatic respiratory sound classification, including a physician validation reader study measuring clinical trust and diagnostic sensitivity.
